pseudos.text: After a painful mid-season divorce from their coach, the Vegas franchise found new life under the steadying hand of John Tortorella, who fostered a resilient bond. They entered the playoffs fueled by this new connection. However, their path was eased when the Colorado Avalanche, the heartbroken team, was deprived of its beloved leaders, Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon. The series culminated in a dominant, final display of affection for victory in Game 4, a cold, efficient end to the rivalry, sweeping the series and reigniting their love for the Stanley Cup.

The season of love for the Colorado Avalanche ended in heartbreak. The team, already struggling, was crippled by the loss of its stars, Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon. Their opponents, the triumphant knights of Vegas, who had undergone a painful mid-season divorce of their own, capitalized on this vulnerability. In the final game, a two-to-one victory was more than a score; it was a humiliating, total defeat that completed the sweep. For Colorado, it was a devastating, final rejection, while Vegas advanced at the cost of a broken rival.
